_account_deploy_limit_pct_note: Account-level deploy cap (via cherrypit.risk). 0 = OFF (default). A positive value (e.g. 50) blocks a LIVE execute_trade whose buying power would push total deployed BP above that percent of account capacity (used + available derivative buying power). Fail-closed: if account state can't be read, the live order is blocked. Enforced only on live submits; a dry-run reports the governor verdict without blocking. Does not affect paper trading.
_position_sizing_note: available_capital_paper_mode is the simulated capital basis for paper mode's risk-cap checks (max_risk_per_trade_pct) -- no real broker balance is consulted in paper mode. Live mode always sources NLV/buying power from tastytrade directly via tt.py get_account_info.
_tastytrade_costs_note: Models tastytrade's real commission schedule (source: tastytrade.com/pricing, 'Commissions & Fees' doc last updated 2026-04-06) for paper-mode cost-adjusted P&L -- see src/costs.py. commission_close_per_contract is 0 by design (tastytrade's distinctive open-only model). clearing/regulatory rates are approximations of pass-through exchange/ORF/FINRA-TAF/SEC fees and change periodically -- re-check the source doc periodically. slippage_frac_of_spread is the fraction of each leg's bid-ask conceded from mid per fill (0.125 = a quarter of the way from mid to the far touch, a worked-combo-limit assumption; was 0.25); slippage_cap_frac_of_mid caps a leg's slippage at that fraction of its mid so deep-OTM junk wings don't dominate.
_symbol_screen_note: Single accept/reject bar for a symbol's soft criteria (replaces the old Tier 1/2/Near-Miss ladder). Hard filters -- price, front-expiration window, open interest, term structure, ATM delta, expected move, weekly cadence, bid/ask spread -- always apply. Each soft criterion below is required at the chosen level: 'pass' uses the strict min_* threshold in strategies.<name>, 'near_miss' uses the looser near_miss_min_* threshold, 'off' drops the criterion entirely. Default is every criterion at 'pass' (the strict bar). 'move_tail' is a two-level switch, not a min/near_miss threshold: 'off' (default, record-only via entry_reviews) or 'veto' (reject a symbol whose historical earnings moves include a blowout quarter -- see move_tail_multiple). See docs/screening-criteria.md.
_move_tail_multiple_note: How many multiples of a name's own mean historical earnings move counts as a 'blowout' quarter for scanner.compute_historical_move_stats' move_tail_veto flag (recorded on every entry_reviews row via symbol_screen; only rejects a symbol when symbol_screen.move_tail is 'veto', off by default until the recorded data supports calibrating this number). 2.0 means any quarter at or above 2x the mean flags the name.
_strat_test_portfolio_note: How the forced-sampling strat_test paper book is split. 'per_strategy' (default) gives each strategy its own book (profile tag strat_test:<strategy>) so each has its own P&L/equity curve and a newly added strategy automatically gets its own stream; 'combined' keeps a single strat_test book. See docs/paper-trading.md and strat_test_harness._book_tag.
_per_name_concentration_is_intended: DECIDED 2026-07-27, do not 'fix' this: every name clearing the accept bar runs EVERY strategy, and the resulting stack of structures on one name is the design, not a risk-control gap. The research question is which strategy is most profitable, which is only answerable if each strategy sees the same names under the same conditions — capping structures per name, or rotating strategies across names, would confound the comparison with selection differences and leave each strategy a different, much smaller sample. An EOD review on 2026-07-27 flagged one accepted name carrying six structures and $2,482 of overnight defined max loss ($1,323 in a single iron_fly) and recommended a per-name cap; that recommendation is declined on the above grounds. What bounds it is that every earnings strategy is DEFINED-RISK (naked was removed for exactly this reason), so the overnight worst case is known at entry — concentrated, not unbounded. The guard actually worth building is the missing CORRELATION guard: several index-correlated names qualifying the same night would collapse supposedly independent bets into one, which is a different problem from one name running the full sweep.
_symbol_watch_note: Config for the forward-preview scan (python -m cherrypick.earnings.symbol_watch refresh) -- purely informational, feeds scout's read-only Earnings page 'Upcoming' section, never a trading decision. Scheduling (whether it runs at all, --days [now TRADING days], time of day) lives in the ORCHESTRATOR's own config, since that's what invokes it. liquid_only (default true) pre-filters the scan to the union of tastytrade's public 'Liquid Symbols' + 'High Options Volume' + 'tasty Earnings' watchlists (tt.py get_watch_universe, one call per pass) BEFORE the expensive per-symbol chain fetch -- scout's own Upcoming section only ever displays rows the scan actually reached, so scanning a name outside that union would waste a broker round trip for nothing never seen. Set false only if a full unfiltered preview is genuinely wanted. tier_thresholds overrides the EarningsEdgeDetection-derived recommended/near_miss/fail bar (symbol_watch.classify_tier) -- a display ranking only, never a gate; omit any key to keep its default (see classify_tier's own _TIER_DEFAULTS for the full list: min_price 10, near_miss_min_price 5, min_iv_rv_ratio 1.25, near_miss_min_iv_rv_ratio 1.00, min_winrate 0.50, near_miss_min_winrate 0.40, min_avg_volume 1500000, near_miss_min_avg_volume 1000000, min_term_structure -0.004, min_expected_move_dollars 0.90, min_combined_open_interest 2000).
_dolt_timeout_note: Bounds on the Dolt path so a cold-starting or compacting server cannot hang the entry scan to its 30-minute external kill. Dolt does not honor MySQL's server-side max_execution_time, so the query phase is bounded client-side. dolthub_connect_timeout caps each connection attempt (seconds). dolt_calendar_timeout_seconds caps the initial entry-calendar fetch (the run fails fast if exceeded). dolt_symbol_timeout_seconds caps a single symbol's Dolt-heavy evaluation, run in a daemon thread and skipped on expiry. entry_scan_budget_seconds is the overall wall-clock backstop after which the scan stops and writes partial results -- keep it well under the scheduled task's kill timeout.
_entry_scan_workers_note: How many symbols the entry scan evaluates concurrently. Each symbol's evaluation is broker-read heavy and independent, and the tt read-through cache is thread-local, so this collapses the scan's wall clock by roughly this factor. Raising it trades against tastytrade API rate limits and one OAuth handshake per concurrent tt.py subprocess. Order building and every paper-DB write stay sequential regardless.
_winrate_lookback_quarters_note: Quarters of earnings history behind BOTH the winrate screen (scanner.compute_winrate) and the realized-move dispersion gate that atm_calendar and double_calendar use — it is not a winrate-only knob, so widening it moves those strategies' gates too. Raised 8 -> 12 on 2026-07-28, measured against live Dolt data first: of 6 recently-screened names 4 returned a full 12 samples and their winrates moved materially, while 2 hit a data wall and degraded gracefully (one held at 3 samples for want of historical option chains, one returns 0 at any lookback). Cost is ~+0.4s per compute_winrate call, and the call happens up to 3x per symbol (rank_strategies plus each calendar strategy's dispersion). Sample size is reported alongside every winrate, so a thin name stays visibly thin.
_exit_after_announcement_note: SAME-SESSION time backstop used by iron_fly, iron_condor and directional_credit_spread: minutes after entry before the position is closed unconditionally with reason 'iv_crush_backstop'. Evaluated BEFORE the profit/stop check, so it wins. TOP-LEVEL, not per-strategy: evaluate_position receives the whole project config (strat_test_harness passes scanner._load_config() straight through), so a copy inside a strategies.<name> block would be ignored. Stated explicitly here because it was previously absent from this file while the code default (240) ran anyway -- an 'overnight hold' could be force-closed four hours after entry with nothing in config to explain it. Raise it past the overnight gap to disable the behaviour in practice.
_correlation_block_list_note: Groups of names not to hold simultaneously — scanner.select_positions takes at most ONE per group, checking already-open positions too. Populated 2026-07-28; it had been empty since the module was written, so the one correlation guard that exists was never actually armed. The group below is the mega-cap index-weight cluster: these carry enough S&P/Nasdaq weight to move with the index and with each other, so holding several overnight is one factor bet wearing the costume of diversification. Deliberately DISTINCT from the per-name concentration decision (running every strategy on ONE accepted name is intended sampling and stays); stacking several CORRELATED names on one night is a different exposure and is what this blocks. A durable sector grouping rather than a dated one, so it keeps working past the week that prompted it. Still a PARTIAL mitigation: it does not measure correlation, it refuses a hand-listed cluster.

iron_fly._wing_width_note: wing_width_credit_multiple is the fallback if iv_rv_ratio can't be refetched at entry time; otherwise superseded by the bands below, scaled to this candidate's own IV/RV ratio (not market-wide VIX -- an earnings move is idiosyncratic to one stock, so its own IV/RV is a more relevant regime signal here than broad market volatility). Reasoned proposal, not backtested for this strategy.
iron_fly._exit_note: Step 3c (market-open-to-close-window) profit-target/stop-loss check via scanner.evaluate_credit_spread_exit, ahead of Step 3's unconditional close-window sweep. Calibrated against earnings-specific short-straddle/iron-butterfly research (not the generic weeks-long income-strategy conventions, which don't transfer to a ~16-hour overnight-gap trade): 50% of max profit as a target, stop at 1.5x credit received. Not backtested for this project specifically.
iron_fly._liquidity_note: Shared liquidity gates (scanner.py's apply_liquidity_gates) -- reasoned starting points, not backtested for this strategy. max_bid_ask_spread_pct at 15% of mid is generous enough not to reject normal earnings-week widening but catches genuinely illiquid chains. min_market_cap at $2B (mid-cap floor) favors names liquid enough that options market-makers stay engaged around an earnings event. min_combined_option_volume (front-month chain-wide daily contract volume, same scope as min_combined_open_interest) is a conservative starting floor.

double_calendar._note: Stricter liquidity/expected-move floors than iron_fly -- execution cost matters more across two expirations, and a single tail-risk surprise hurts a debit trade more than iron_fly's width-defined max loss. Reasoned starting points, not backtested for this strategy.
double_calendar._exit_note: Calibrated against published backtests/practitioner guidance, not backtested for this strategy specifically: profit target of 20-30% of max profit shows improved profitability and less time-at-risk in structured studies (25% used as the midpoint); 5-7 DTE front-month exit is described as non-negotiable since gamma risk on a short ATM option overwhelms theta benefit inside that window (5 used, not the looser 2-3 day figure); stop_loss_pct_of_debit is a whole-position backstop for when the spread's value round-trips back toward the entry debit, separate from leg_stop_delta_abs which handles a single threatened side.

iron_condor._note: Same credit-spread-plus-wings shape as iron_fly, but short strikes sit at the expected-move boundary (1.0x, same convention as double_calendar/expected_move_butterfly) instead of ATM -- backtests show a wider profit zone, lower credit, and a materially different historical win rate than iron fly. Not backtested for this project's specific implementation.
iron_condor._exit_note: Step 3c (market-open-to-close-window) profit-target/stop-loss check via scanner.evaluate_credit_spread_exit, same convention and rationale as iron_fly's -- 50% of max profit target, 1.5x credit stop. Not backtested for this project specifically.

atm_calendar._note: Sell a front-month ATM call, buy the same strike in a later monthly expiration -- same front/back term-structure edge as double_calendar, one option type instead of two, always the call side (config-fixed, not skew-selected -- call/put ATM calendars perform virtually identically). Always closes as a single 2-leg unit (legs_json only, never trade_legs), unlike double_calendar's independently-closeable sides. No expected-move-boundary filter -- this is a pure ATM term-structure play, not targeting where the stock lands. Reasoned starting points, not backtested for this strategy.
atm_calendar._exit_note: Same researched-convention shape as double_calendar's: profit target at 25-30% of max profit (midpoint of the 20-75% range described in practitioner guidance), stop when the debit has roughly doubled (stop_loss_pct_of_debit=1.0, matching evaluate_debit_spread_exit's convention -- note this is looser than expected_move_butterfly's 0.40 since a calendar's decay profile is slower-resolving), 5-day time-exit before front expiration for the same gamma-risk-overwhelms-theta reasoning as double_calendar's. Not backtested for this project specifically.

directional_credit_spread._note: Single-sided vertical credit spread (put spread if bullish, call spread if bearish), sold on whichever side the 25-delta risk reversal shows richer (expected_move_butterfly.select_side(), reused as-is -- min_skew_abs/skew_delta_target share that module's meaning). Genuinely new strike-selection convention for this project: the short strike is chosen so BREAKEVEN (short strike minus/plus credit received) lands at the expected-move boundary, not the strike itself -- see directional_credit_spread.py's _select_short_strike. Same overnight-gap hold model and Step 3/3c close mechanism as iron_fly/iron_condor. Reasoned starting points, not backtested for this strategy.
directional_credit_spread._exit_note: Step 3c (market-open-to-close-window) profit-target/stop-loss check via scanner.evaluate_credit_spread_exit, same convention and rationale as iron_fly's/iron_condor's -- 50% of max profit target, 1.5x credit stop. Not backtested for this project specifically.

broken_wing_butterfly._note: Body-anchored (no ATM leg): 2 short contracts at the expected-move strike (the body, side picked via a 25-delta risk reversal), protected by a narrow long wing toward current price and a wide long wing away from it, both sized directly off the body strike -- NOT expected_move_butterfly's 1-2-1 ATM/short/far shape. Near wing width scales per-candidate off the body leg's own premium via the IV/RV-banded wing_width_multiple_low/_mid/_high bands (deliberately smaller than iron_fly's 2.5/3.0/3.5, since this sizes a single-leg premium, not a straddle credit); far wing is wide_wing_multiple times the near wing. Reasoned starting point, not backtested for this strategy.
broken_wing_butterfly._credit_only_note: get_order hard-rejects (net_debit_positive_credit_required) any candidate that doesn't price out to a net credit or breakeven -- if a candidate's real premiums land as a net debit at these wing widths, they didn't buy back enough premium to finance the position, so it's rejected outright rather than entered as a smaller-debit butterfly. Raise wide_wing_multiple or the wing_width_multiple_* bands if too many real candidates are being rejected this way.
broken_wing_butterfly._exit_note: Exit order for this strategy: (1) a per-leg delta stop, leg_stop_delta_abs, code default 0.60; (2) scanner.evaluate_credit_spread_exit -- the CREDIT-spread exit, not the debit one, despite the structure pricing as a net debit. That function reads profit_target_pct and stop_loss_credit_multiple (set explicitly below; code defaults are 0.10/2.0x if omitted). Not backtested for this project specifically.
